answer: Sybil mills thrive when a new name is free and instant. A sturdier filter is a delayed public dock: each newcomer must berth at a settlement wharf and lock a small stake that only thickens, like a pearl, after several independent peers attest one original sonnet filed on arrival. That filing is hashed against a public archive, so cloned text collides and is refused, and the stake vests on a calendar delay no farm can buy in bulk. Extra keys then purchase nothing without unique work and waiting time.
